ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: The History of Human Skin from Middle Ages to the Present Description: The surface of human body has a deep history. In this course we will study the transition from medieval to modern ideas about skin, especially in relation to human difference and identity. We will read and discuss recent scholarship on the history of: skin in Western medicine; skin and beauty, blushing, cosmetics, and tanning; skin color and the formation of racism; skin in premodern China; scarification in West African cultures and in the Atlantic world; and the global circulation of tattooing. By encompassing diverse fields such as the history of medicine, art history, cultural history, legal history, the history of race and slavery, and the history of religion, this course provides a broad introduction to historical interpretation. Assignments include short essays, a midterm exam, and a research paper.
